author: Linnaeus, 1758

months.note: 번식지에서는 5~7월에 알을 낳고, 한 해 두 번 번식한다.

summary: 우리나라 전역에 불규칙하게 찾아오는 흔하지 않은 겨울새로, 주로 나무 위에서 지낸다. 여름에는 암수가 함께 지내고 가을과 겨울에는 작은 무리를 짓는다. 식물의 씨앗과 어린잎, 곤충 등을 먹는다. 아무르강 하류, 우수리, 사할린 등지에서 번식하며, 관목 가지에 나무껍질과 풀뿌리로 컵 모양 둥지를 짓고 한배에 알을 4~6개 낳는다.

points.en: red cheeks, throat and upper breast

art.subject: Eurasian Bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula), adult male of the grey-bellied form usual in Korea in winter, November to March: glossy blue-black cap from the forehead to the nape, with black also around the base of the bill and on the chin; cheeks, ear coverts, throat and upper breast rose-red; nape, mantle and back clean ash-grey; wings glossy black with a broad pale grey band across the greater coverts; rump pure white; lower breast, belly and flanks pale grey washed rosy-pink; undertail coverts white; tail glossy blue-black. Bill very short, deep and rounded, black; iris dark brown; legs dark brown.
art.pose: perched on a tree branch, eating seeds
art.scene: Korean winter trees and shrubs with bare branches; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male winter, side view perched: glossy black cap and chin, rose-red cheeks, throat and upper breast, grey back, pale grey belly washed rosy, black wings with a pale grey bar, black wingtips and tail
adult male winter, back view perched: black cap, clean grey back, pale grey wing-bar, white rump, glossy black wings and tail
adult female, side view perched: same black cap, black wings with grey bar and black tail, but cheeks and underparts warm greyish-brown and back brownish-grey, white rump
art.build: Plump, bull-necked finch, 15cm, a little bigger than a sparrow and much rounder. Large rounded head with no crest and almost no visible neck. Bill very short, deep and stubby with a strongly rounded culmen, much shorter than the head. Legs short, dark brown. Sits quietly in trees and shrubs, often leaning or hanging from twigs to take buds and seeds. At rest the wingtips reach only the base of the tail. Tail medium length, square-ended or slightly notched, all black. In flight the white rump stands out between the grey back and the black tail.
avoid: Do not paint the whole underparts orange-red down to the vent; on Korean birds the red stops at the upper breast and the belly is pale grey washed pink.
Do not extend the black over the cheeks; black covers only the cap, the bill base and the chin, and the male's cheeks are red.
Do not give it a pointed or long bill; it is short, stubby and swollen.
Do not leave out the white rump, and do not add white in the tail or extra wing-bars.
